questions.question: Who discovered a principle that states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Archimedes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The principle that states that the buoyant force on an object is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object is known as** Archimedes' Principle.**
 
• Archimedes' Principle is attributed to Archimedes of Syracuse, **a Greek mathematician** and inventor who lived from approximately 287 to 212 BCE.
 
• The principle was described in his work **"On Floating Bodies."**
 
• This principle is** fundamental in fluid mechanics** and **explains why objects float or sink in fluids**.
 
• The** formula** for Archimedes' principle is** FB = ρVg,** where:
 
 
• FB: is the buoyant force 
 
• ρ: is the density of the fluid 
 
• V: is the volume of the object that is submerged or the volume

questions.question:
Which of the following equation of motion is correct?

I. v = (u/2) + at

II. s = 2ut + at²
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither I nor II**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***v = u + at*** is the first equation of motion.

 
 
• It is the equation of motion-time relation__.
 
• In this ​v=u+at equation,
 __
 
• u is the initial velocity
 
• v is the final velocity
 
• a is acceleration
 
• t is the time period
 
 
 
• The given equation is derived from the acceleration point of view. (It can also be derived from velocity and time graphs)
 
 
 
• ***s = ut + 1over2 at²***

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8e6412eaa10e855ffc4fb5c50220b89d8165c04af44bd58fcf4a3d95e0d6e7a.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• In the case of uniform acceleration, there are three equations of motion which are also known as the laws of constant acceleration.
 
• The three equations are,
 
 
• ​v=u+at
 
• v² = u² + 2as\ or \ v² - u² = 2as​
 
• s = ut + {1over{2}}at² 
 
 
 
• where, s = displacement; u = initial velocity; v = final velocity; a = acceleration; t = time of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• These equations are referred to as SUVAT equations where SUVAT stands for displacement (s), initial velocity (u), final velocity (v), acceleration (a) and time (T).​

questions.question: Which wave oscillates parallel to the motion of the sound wave?

__
 
• In Longitudinal waves, the particles of the medium** oscillate parallel to the direction of the wave**.
 
• Longitudinal waves r**equire a medium(solid, liquid, or gas)** to propagate.
 
• The speed of the wave** depends upon the properties of the medium** such as density and elasticity.
 
• Common examples of Longitudinal waves are **sound waves in air, Seismic-P waves, and waves in springs**.

questions.question: Whose law states that at a junction in an electric circuit, the sum of the currents flowing into the junction is equal to the sum of the currents flowing out of the junction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gustav Robert Kirchhoff.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Kirchhoff's first law** is also known as** Kirchhoff's Junction Rule, Kirchhoff's Point Rule, Kirchhoff's Nodal Rule, and Kirchhoff's Current Law.**
 
• According to the law, the s**um of the currents going into **and** out of any circuit junction** must be **equal.**
 
• This is because it has no other place to go and **no charge is lost.**
 
• The **algebraic sum of ALL the currents entering and leaving** a junction must be **equal to zero **as:
 
 
• Σ IIₙ = Σ IOᵤₜ
 
 
 
• Since** there is no current loss** surrounding the junction, Kirchhoff's theory is also known as the **"Conservation of Charge."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Michael Faraday:**

 
 
• According to Faraday's first law of **electromagnetic induction**, an **electromotive force** is always induced whenever a **conductor **is subjected to a changing **magnetic field.**
 
 
 
• **Georg Simon Ohm:**
 
 
• Ohm found that there is a direct proportionality between the **potential difference (voltage) **applied across a** conductor and the resultant electric current.**
 
• This is called **Ohm's law. **
 
 
 
• **Victor Francis Hess:**
 
 
• Victor Hess made the **1912 discovery of cosmic rays **through balloon experiments.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Volume – Meter.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A unit of volume** is a measure used to quantify the extent of an object or space in three dimensions, known as **capacity**.
 
• These units are utilized to specify the volume of various substances such as fluids or bulk goods, including water, rice, sugar, grain, or flour.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI),** the base unit for measuring length is the **meter**. Consequently, the SI unit of volume is the **cubic meter (m³)**, which is a derived unit.
 
• The cubic meter represents the volume of a cube with edges each measuring one meter in length.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **International System of Units (SI) **is a globally recognized system of measurement standards. It comprises seven base SI units:

 
 
• **Meter (m)**: The unit of length
 
• **Kilogram (kg)**: The unit of mass
 
• **Ampere (A)**: The unit of electric current
 
• **Second (s)** : The unit of time
 
• **Kelvin (K)**: The unit of thermodynamic temperature
 
• **Mole (mol)**: The unit of amount of substance 
 
• **Candela (cd)**: The unit of luminous intensity
 
 
 
• Derived SI units are formed by combining these base units according to algebraic rules. Examples of derived units include the Newton (N) for force, the Pascal (Pa) for pressure, and the Joule (J) for energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for determining the value of 1 ampere.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A = 1C/s**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **1 ampere** is defined as the amount of current that flows when **1 coulomb (C) of charge passes a point in 1 second (s)**.
 
• The formula for current (I) is given by **I = Q / t**, where 'I' is the current in amperes, 'Q' is the charge in coulombs, and 't' is the time in seconds.
 
• According to the options provided, **Option 2: A = 1C/s** correctly represents this relationship.
 
• This definition is fundamental in the field of electromagnetism and is used to standardize measurements of electric current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **ampere** is one of the seven base units in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• It is named after the French physicist **André-Marie Ampère**, who is considered one of the founders of the science of electromagnetism.
 
• The ampere is a crucial unit in electrical and electronic engineering, affecting everything from circuit design to power distribution.
 
• Modern definitions of units like the ampere rely on fundamental physical constants, ensuring consistency and precision in scientific measurements.

__
 
• The conversion formula from Fahrenheit to Celsius is:
 
• C = 5/9 (F - 32) = 5/9 (59 - 32) = 5/9 × 27 = 15°c

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Understanding how to convert temperatures between these scales is useful for international communication and travel.

• Before a yo-yo is released, it is held at a certain height, giving it** gravitational** potential energy.
 
• This energy is converted into kinetic energy as the yo-yo is released and starts to move.
 
• Potential energy is a fundamental concept in physics, often contrasted with kinetic energy, which is the energy of motion.

• **Chemical energy**: This is the energy stored in the bonds of** chemical compounds**. Ex-battery
 
• **Light energy**: This is the energy carried by light waves. ex-laser

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for the moment of inertia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I = mr²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The formula for the moment of inertia is the **“sum of the product of mass” **of each particle with the “square of its distance from the axis of the rotation”.
 
• The formula of Moment of Inertia is expressed as** I = Σ miri2**.
 
• **The moment of inertia **is a measure of a body's resistance to angular acceleration, calculated as the sum of each particle's mass multiplied by the square of its distance from the axis of rotation.
 
• In simpler terms, it determines how much torque is required to achieve a given angular acceleration about a rotational axis.
 
• Also referred to as angular mass or rotational inertia, the moment of inertia is measured in kilograms times square meters (kg m²).
 
• Similar to mass in linear motion, it quantifies a body's resistance to changes in its rotational motion and remains constant for a rigid frame and a particular axis of rotation.

questions.question: Which part of the bifocal lens facilitates near vision?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lower part with convex lens**__

__
 
• The **lower part with convex lens** in a bifocal lens facilitates near vision.
 
• Bifocal lenses are designed to correct both near and distant vision issues.
 
• The **upper part** of the bifocal lens is typically for **distance vision**, while the **lower part** is for **near vision**.
 
• This design allows individuals to see clearly at different distances without needing to switch between different pairs of glasses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• They are particularly useful for people with presbyopia, a condition that affects near vision as people age.
 
• Modern variations include **progressive lenses**, which provide a gradient of varying lens powers for a smoother transition between near and far vision.
 
• Regular eye check-ups are essential to ensure that the prescription for bifocal lenses remains accurate.

questions.question: When did Heinrich Hertz discover the photoelectric effect and observe that shining ultraviolet light on the electrodes caused a change in voltage between them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1887**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Heinrich Hertz, a German physicist,** conducted experiments in the late 19th century to investigate** electromagnetic waves**.
 
• **In 1887, Hertz discovered the photoelectric effect **while studying the behavior of electromagnetic waves.
 
• Hertz’s work laid the groundwork for understanding the **quantum nature of light** and the concept of **wave–particle duality.**
 
• His observations were consistent with the idea that light consists of **discrete packets of energy (later called photons).**
 
• Hertz’s experiments provided experimental evidence for the existence of electromagnetic waves predicted by Maxwell’s theory.
 
• His work influenced Max Planck, who later introduced the concept of **quantization of energy **to explain the photoelectric effect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Photoelectric Effect**

 
• The photoelectric effect refers to the phenomenon where** light (photons) **striking a material surface causes the emission of** electrons **from that surface.
 
• When light of sufficient energy** (usually ultraviolet or higher frequencies) **falls on a metal surface, **electrons **are ejected from the metal.
 
• The **kinetic energy** of the emitted electrons depends on the** frequency (color) **of the incident light.
 
• There is a** threshold frequency**, below this frequency, **no photoemission occurs,** regardless of light intensity.
 
• The number of** emitted electrons** is proportional to the **intensity (brightness) of the light.**

questions.question: Which of the following rule is used to find the direction of magnetic field associated with a current carrying conductor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maxwell's corkscrew rule.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Maxwell's corkscrew rule:

 
 
• Maxwell’s corkscrew rule describes the relationship between the direction of the electric current and that of the magnetic field lines associated with it.
 
• As the name suggests the direction in which the screw moves and the direction in which its handle rotates or turns correspond to the directions of the current and the field lines.
 
• Imagine a right-handed corkscrew lying with its axis coinciding with the current-carrying wire.
 
• It is now rotated such that it advances in the direction of the current, and then the direction in which the screw rotates gives the direction of the magnetic field____.__

questions.question: 1 kilowatt is equivalent to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__3600KJ/h__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 1 kilowatt is equivalent to 3600 kJ/h .This is because 1 kilowatt is equal to **1000** **joules** **per** **second**, and there are 3600 seconds in an hour (60 seconds/minute * 60 minutes/hour). Therefore, 1 kilowatt is equal to **1000** **joules/second** * 3600 seconds/hour, resulting in 3600 kJ/h.
 
• Option 1 :3600 kJ/h: This is the energy equivalent to 1 kilowatt-hour (kWh). Since 1 kWh = **3600** **kJ**, this option is equivalent to **1** **kW**.
 
• Option 2: 3600 calorie: This is not directly related to kilowatts. Calories are a unit of energy, but they're not the SI unit like joules or kilojoules.
 
• Option 3: 7200 kJ/h: This would be equivalent to 2 kilowatts (kW) for an hour, not 1 kW.
 
• Option 4: This is not correct. 1 kilowatt is equivalent to 1000 watts, which is equal to 1000 joules per second. So, 1 kW would be equal to 3600 kJ/h.

 
• The SI unit of energy is same as that of work, which is **joule** **(J).**

questions.question: Identify the correct statement about gravity.

options.text: The unit of g is the same as that of velocity.
The unit of g is the same as that of friction.
The unit of g is the same as that of mass.
The unit of g is the same as that of acceleration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 4) __**The unit of g is the same as that of acceleration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The force of attraction exerted by the earth on a body is called **gravitational pull or gravity.**
 
• We know that when a force acts on a body, it produces acceleration. Therefore, a body under the effect of gravitational pull must accelerate.
 
• The acceleration produced in the motion of a body under the effect of gravity is called **acceleration due to gravity, it is denoted by g and is measured in m/s² .**
 
• The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is **9.81 m/s² ​.**
 
• ** Statements 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect** because: 
 
 
• 1) **Velocity** is measured in **m/s,** not m/s2; 
 
• 2)** Friction** doesn't have a unit of acceleration, it's a force measured in **Newtons**; 
 
• 3) **Mass** is measured in **kilograms** (kg), not in terms of acceleration.
 
 
 
• Since** g** is measured in** m/s****²** and the same with acceleration, so both have same unit. **Hence option 4 is correct**

questions.question: Which physical theory explains the generation of thrust by rocket engines, jet engines and deflating balloons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton’s laws of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Newton's third law states that **"For every action, there is an equal but opposite reaction"**.

 
 
• Example: **Thrust generation in the rocket propulsion rocket engines, jet engines, and deflating balloons**.
 
 
 
• When burn-out fuel mixture is thrown in the back direction with high velocity then in the reaction a forward thrust is generated which pushes the rocket in a forward direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Newton’s First Law of Motion: 

__
 
• The first law is the law of Inertia.
 
• According to it, if a body is at rest will remain at rest, and if the body is in motion will remain in motion unless an external force is applied to it.
 
• An example is: The motion of a ball falling down through the atmosphere

Newtons Second Law:

 
• Newton's second law of motion is F = ma, where m is the mass of an object and a is the acceleration.
 
• It states that the "Rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the external force applied to that body.
 
• An example of Newton's 2nd law is riding your bicycle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Faraday’s laws of electromagnetic induction**- It states that whenever a conductor is placed in a varying magnetic field, an electromotive force is induced.
 
• **Exclusion principle**- The principle states that in a single atom no two electrons will have an identical set or the same quantum numbers.
